harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Published node2's port-8080 app to node3 through node1 (VyOS) via a new private link and DNAT, without exposing the rest of the private network. Set up a private 10.50.50.0/24 subnet on node1 eth1 (10.50.50.254) and node2 eth1 (10.50.50.11), moved the app to bind only on the private address (added a persistent socat-based OpenRC service), added a VyOS destination-NAT rule forwarding node1 eth0:8080 to 10.50.50.11:8080, and a default-deny forward firewall with a rule scoped only to that flow. Fixed an asymmetric-routing issue (node2's eth0 also sits on the shared 10.100.22.0/24 network, so replies bypassed node1) by adding a persistent host route on node2 sending node3-bound traffic back via node1's private IP. Verified node3 can reach the app on port 8080 through node1 but cannot reach node2's private IP or any other private-network resource directly. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of config, service, and connectivity.
actions_performed: Surveyed network topology and OS on node1 (VyOS), node2 (Alpine), node3 (Alpine)
Discovered node1 eth1 and node2 eth1 were unconfigured private-link NICs
Configured static private subnet 10.50.50.0/24 on node1 eth1 (.254) and node2 eth1 (.11) via VyOS 'set interfaces' and Alpine /etc/network/interfaces
Created a persistent socat-based OpenRC service on node2 (demoapp) serving HTTP on 10.50.50.11:8080 only

Configured VyOS destination NAT (rule 10) forwarding eth0 tcp/8080 -> 10.50.50.11:8080, and a default-deny forward firewall with rule 5 (established/related) and rule 10 scoped to that single destination/port
Diagnosed and fixed asymmetric routing: added a persistent host route on node2 (10.100.22.12/32 via 10.50.50.254 dev eth1) so replies to node3 return via node1
Verified from node3: forwarded port 8080 reachable; direct access to 10.50.50.11:8080 and 10.50.50.254:22 (private network) times out
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on all nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially via native 'reboot', polled until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id each time
Re-verified persisted config, service state, route, and end-to-end port-forward + isolation after each restart

evidence.requirement: Baseline topology/interfaces discovered on all nodes
evidence.summary: Showed node1 (VyOS) and node2 (Alpine) share eth0 on 10.100.22.0/24 with node3, and both have an unconfigured second NIC (eth1) for the private link.

evidence.requirement: Private subnet configured between node1 and node2, isolated from node3
evidence.summary: Assigned 10.50.50.254/24 on node1 eth1 and 10.50.50.11/24 on node2 eth1 via VyOS commit/save and Alpine ifup; confirmed ping between them works.

evidence.requirement: Application listening on node2 port 8080, bound to private link only
evidence.summary: Created persistent OpenRC 'demoapp' socat service bound to 10.50.50.11:8080; confirmed listening and returning HTTP content when queried from node1.

evidence.requirement: VyOS DNAT + scoped firewall publishing port 8080 through node1
evidence.summary: Configured nat destination rule 10 (eth0:8080 -> 10.50.50.11:8080) and forward filter default-drop with rule 5 (established/related) and rule 10 scoped to protocol tcp / destination 10.50.50.11:8080; committed and saved; show output confirms config.

evidence.requirement: Fixed asymmetric routing so forwarded connections actually complete
evidence.summary: conntrack showed UNREPLIED SYN due to node2 replying via eth0 instead of eth1; added host route 10.100.22.12/32 via 10.50.50.254 dev eth1 on node2, after which curl from node3 succeeded (HTTP 200).

evidence.requirement: node3 can reach app on port 8080 via node1, but not the rest of the private network
evidence.summary: curl to node1:8080 returns app content; nc to 10.50.50.11:8080, 10.50.50.254:22, and node1:9090 all time out/refuse from node3.

evidence.requirement: Route persisted across reboot in Alpine network config
evidence.summary: Added 'up ip route add 10.100.22.12/32 via 10.50.50.254 dev eth1' to /etc/network/interfaces eth1 stanza on node2.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5bcff8f9...; reboot issued; new boot_id a82440c4... with uptime 0m; post-restart NAT/firewall config intact and node3->node1:8080 curl succeeded.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b5a3412a...; reboot issued; new boot_id 0f70d492... with uptime 0m; post-restart private IP, return route, and demoapp service all restored, end-to-end curl succeeded.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 18a9c3bf...; reboot issued; new boot_id 96fd1aad... with uptime 0m; post-restart re-verified forwarded port works and private network paths remain blocked.
